cohort: 830 neonates born alive, of unique pregnancy, <2000 g from October 1999 to July 2013 at the Maternity of Hospital - Irmandade Santa Casa de Misericórdia de São Paulo, Brazil
finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with better neonatal outcomes than cesarean delivery in neonates weighing 1000-2000g, but cesarean delivery was associated with better outcomes in neonates <1000g.
mod_finding: Neonates born via vaginal delivery had a higher incidence of respiratory distress syndrome and intraventricular hemorrhage across all weight groups.
